chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, who said:

I was in the presence of Abī Jaʿfar al-Thānī (عليه السلام) when Ṣāliḥ ibn Muḥammad ibn Sahl entered upon him, and he used to administer the waqf for him in Qumm. He said, “O my master, release me from liability for ten thousand, for I have spent it.” So he said to him, “You are released.”

Then when Ṣāliḥ left, Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) said: “One of them pounces upon the wealth that is the right of the family of Muḥammad, their orphans, their needy ones, their poor ones, and their stranded travelers, and takes it; then he comes to me saying, ‘Release me from liability.’ Do you think he supposed that I would say, ‘I will not do so’? By Allah, Allah will surely question them on the Day of Resurrection about that with an intense questioning.”

key_terms.أَمْوَالِ حَقِّ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: the wealth belonging to the rightful due of the family of Muḥammad
key_terms.أَيْتَامِهِمْ: their orphans, among the designated beneficiaries
key_terms.الْوَقْفَ: the endowment or dedicated property being administered
key_terms.فِي حِلٍّ: released from liability or declared absolved
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection when accountability will occur

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about misusing the financial rights of Āl Muḥammad and khums-related funds?
ai.summary: This hadith concerns liability regarding funds belonging to the rights of Āl Muḥammad and designated beneficiaries such as orphans, the needy, the poor, and stranded travelers. Although the Imam (عليه السلام) outwardly told the man he was released, he then declared that Allah will intensely question those who seize such wealth on the Day of Resurrection.
